texts: The incorrect statement is that the signs and symptoms of an ASD are not related to the direction or magnitude of the shunt: D.
They follow the shunt closely: a small left-to-right shunt is silent, a large one enlarges the right heart and causes breathlessness and arrhythmia, and a reversed shunt causes cyanosis.
Defects under 6 mm almost always close or become restrictive on their own, those of 6 to 8 mm may still do so after age 5, and those over 8 mm can grow during childhood.
In adults, an episode of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation may be the first presentation.
In the picture, the sailor is calm by the trickle, breathless by the flood and blue-lipped by the reversed flow.
Memory hook: the signs follow the water.
